methodological_rigor.justification: Competent retrospective cohort design with appropriate use of propensity score matching (1:1 ratio, caliper 0.02) to control confounding between ICI cross-line and non-cross-line groups. However, single-center enrollment, lack of control group, and absence of pre-specified analyses or sensitivity testing represent identifiable gaps. Statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, log-rank tests) are standard but lack multiplicity correction or formal power calculation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study evaluating ICI-based treatments across three lines of therapy in pMMR/MSS mCRC, a common malignancy with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Directly addresses real-world clinical practice and identifies ICI+TKI as emerging strategy in 3L+ setting with survival benefit (median OS 11.9 months). Authors explicitly identify gap in routine clinical practice data, filling documented need.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE framework largely followed with transparent Methods section including inclusion/exclusion criteria, outcome definitions (RECIST 1.1, CTCAE 5.0), and statistical approach. Significant gaps in data availability: no public data deposition statement provided; PD-L1 and genomic profiling unavailable for most patients; MSI/MMR testing methods mentioned but not standardized across cohort. Authors acknowledge limitations but provide no data-sharing plan.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim first real-world study of ICI-based treatment patterns across all lines in pMMR/MSS mCRC. Meaningful extension of randomized trial data (AtezoTRIBE, CheckMate 9X8) into heavily treated 3L+ population, with novel documentation of ICI+TKI dominance (77.7%) in this cohort. However, represents incremental confirmation of known treatment evolution rather than discovery of new mechanism or unexpected efficacy signal.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear structure, logical flow from Methods through Discussion, and effective use of tables (safety profile stratified by treatment line) and figures (Kaplan-Meier curves, treatment regimen breakdown). Discussion appropriately contextualizes results against published trials and acknowledges study limitations. Minor redundancy in safety reporting across multiple sections.

key_strengths: Addresses documented gap in real-world ICI combination data for pMMR/MSS mCRC across multiple treatment lines
Appropriate propensity score matching methodology to control confounding in ICI cross-line therapy analysis
Clear clinical relevance with practical guidance on treatment sequencing (chemotherapy 1L/2L, ICI+TKI 3L+)
Comprehensive safety reporting with manageable adverse event profile across combination regimens
Well-written with transparent acknowledgment of limitations including single-center design and missing biomarkers
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with inherent selection and recall bias limits generalizability of real-world findings
ICI cross-line therapy primary finding (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.39–1.14, P=0.123) lacks statistical significance after PSM
Critical missing data: PD-L1 status and genomic profiling unavailable for majority of cohort, hindering biomarker-driven subgroup identification
No data availability statement or deposition plan; reproducibility limited by retrospective nature and lack of code sharing
Survival outcomes in 3L+ setting (11.4% ORR, 4.7-month PFS) do not substantially exceed historical single-agent TKI comparators discussed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid clinical observational study appropriate for Tier 3 journals (Cancers, Frontiers in Oncology) with competent methodology and clear translational implications, but limited by single-center design, retrospective bias, and lack of statistical significance for key ICI cross-line hypothesis. Missing biomarker annotation and data availability statement prevent Tier 2 placement despite direct clinical relevance.
